title: Self-Instruct: Aligning LMs with Self-Generated Instructions
hook: Instead of paying humans to write instruction data, have the model write its own — bootstrap instructions, inputs, and outputs from its own generations, filter, and fine-tune.
key_points: A bootstrapping loop generates instructions, inputs, and outputs from the model's own output, then filters and fine-tunes on them.
Applied to GPT-3, it gives a 33% absolute gain on Super-NaturalInstructions.
Reaches performance on par with InstructGPT-001 using almost no human-labeled data.
Only a 5% absolute gap behind InstructGPT-001 on expert-written novel-task instructions.
content_html: Yizhong Wang, Yeganeh Kordi, Swaroop Mishra, and colleagues asked whether a model could supply its own instruction-tuning data instead of relying on costly human labels. Their answer, Self-Instruct, is a bootstrapping framework that prompts the model to generate new instructions along with matching inputs and outputs, filters the results, and fine-tunes the model on what survives. Applied to GPT-3, it delivered a 33% absolute improvement on Super-NaturalInstructions and reached performance on par with InstructGPT-001.
extra_html:
How it works

The loop starts from a small seed set of tasks and asks the model to generate fresh instructions, then to produce the corresponding inputs and outputs. A filtering step drops low-quality or redundant examples before the kept data is folded back in to fine-tune the model. Because the data comes almost entirely from the model itself, the method needs nearly no human-labeled examples.

Why it matters

Self-Instruct showed that the expensive part of instruction tuning — writing the data — could be largely automated. The authors report that the GPT-3 model tuned this way matched InstructGPT-001 and sat only about 5% absolute behind it on expert-written novel-task instructions, a strong result for an approach with almost no human supervision. It became a template for the synthetic-data pipelines used to align many later models.

related.title: FLAN: Instruction Tuning
related.hook: Teach a model to follow many tasks phrased as plain instructions, and it learns to follow instructions for tasks it never saw — zero-shot.

related.title: InstructGPT: Aligning LMs with Human Feedback (RLHF)
related.hook: A smaller model people actually like beats a bigger one they don't. InstructGPT used human preferences to make a model follow instructions — the recipe behind ChatGPT.

flashcards.prompt: What does the Self-Instruct bootstrapping loop do?

flashcards.prompt: What is the key advantage of Self-Instruct over standard instruction tuning?

choices.text: The data comes almost entirely from the model itself, needing nearly no human labels
It requires a larger model to generate the instructions
It removes the fine-tuning step altogether
